title: What 7 killed products taught Tibo: recurring use, timing, self-serve, unit economics
summary: Tibo walks through seven products he shut down (ProductLift, Tweet Butler, ConvertRec, GeoLeads, AnimStats, Daily Nuggets and others) and the lesson each taught. The recurring themes are daily/weekly use, timing, avoiding custom work, choosing the right customer type, and unit economics. He argues fast, cheap failures are the best education.

principles.text: Build for recurring use. A problem people only have once is not a SaaS.
principles.quote: You can't build a recurring business on something people need once.

principles.text: Monthly subscriptions need daily or weekly use cases; quarterly use causes brutal churn.
principles.quote: Monthly subscriptions need high frequency use cases.

principles.text: Timing can kill a good idea: wait until the underlying technology is ready.
principles.quote: Some ideas are just 2 years too early. That doesn't make them bad ideas. It makes them bad ideas for right now.

principles.text: If every customer needs custom work, you've built an agency, not a product.
principles.quote: If a product can't work without me, it's not a product, it’s a service.

principles.text: Customer type matters more than revenue; keep products self-service and avoid high-touch enterprise clients.
principles.quote: $1k MRR from the wrong customers is worse than $0 MRR.

principles.text: Kill failing products fast; cheap, quick failures are the best education.
